passage:
Dear Aunt Lisa,

Thank you so much for the family photo album you sent! I was thrilled to flip through it and relive all those childhood memories. The pictures of our summer trips to the lake house brought tears to my eyes—especially the one of us kids building that lopsided sandcastle. I've been meaning to organize a family reunion, and your gift inspired me to finally do it. We've all scattered over the years, but it's time to bring everyone together.

I started planning right away. I picked a weekend in July at the old lake house in Muskoka, Ontario—it's still in the family, right? I called Mom, and she's excited; Uncle Tom said he'd drive up from Toronto with his barbecue gear. We could have a big potluck, games on the beach, and share stories late into the night. Remember how Grandma used to tell ghost stories that scared us silly? I found her old recipe book in the album, so I'll make her famous blueberry pie.

The drive to check on the lake house last weekend was nostalgic. The road winds through pine forests just like always, but the dock has seen better days—rotten boards and all. I spent the afternoon patching it up with some lumber from town. The water was crystal clear, perfect for swimming, though a family of loons kept us company with their eerie calls. I sat on the porch at sunset, thinking about how you and I used to fish there, whispering secrets while waiting for a bite.

On the way home, I stopped in the nearby town of Bracebridge for supplies. It hasn't changed much: the same ice cream shop where we'd get double scoops after a day in the sun. I bought some local maple syrup to add to the reunion menu. Seeing the familiar streets made me miss our family bond more than ever. You've always been the glue holding us together, Aunt Lisa, with your letters and calls keeping everyone updated.

Now that I'm back in Vancouver, the city's hustle feels louder than usual. Your album reminded me how precious these connections are. So, what do you think about heading the reunion committee with me? We have three months to pull it off—I could visit you in Ottawa first to brainstorm. I've got vacation time saved from my teaching job, enough for a road trip east. Maybe we could stop at some roadside diners along the way, just like old times. Let me know your thoughts!

Love,
Sarah
